summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her third cycle of R-ICE chemotherapy for EBV-positive classical Hodgkin lymphoma with skull base and nasopharyngeal involvement, following a good response after two prior cycles. She tolerated treatment with mild somnolence from ifosfamide, which resolved, and required a single unit of packed red blood cells due to anemia. Her white blood cell and platelet counts remained low but stable, without infection. An MRI showed continued regression of the skull base mass with no new intracranial lesions. She was discharged home with instructions to start filgrastim, monitor blood glucose due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia, and follow up for blood counts and transplant evaluation. Her chronic conditions, including CVID, diabetes, and back pain, were managed throughout.
